tagline: Australia's river city — the CityCat network is the spine of inner-Brisbane public transport, now going all-electric.
summary: Brisbane is built around its winding tidal river, and the CityCat / CityHopper ferry network is the spine of inner-city public transport — roughly 25 terminals from UQ St Lucia through the CBD to Northshore Hamilton carrying about 5 million trips a year, ticketed through Translink. Brisbane City Council has committed to an all-electric CityCat fleet and the city is preparing to host the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games. Every core river leg is sheltered and well inside Pioneer II range, making Brisbane a strong public-transport waterway market with a clear decarbonization mandate and a major-event catalyst.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II covers the entire Brisbane River CityCat network — every core reach from UQ St Lucia to Northshore Hamilton is sheltered and well inside the 70nm range.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) could extend to longer Moreton Bay or SE-Queensland coastal trunks (e.g. toward the bay islands or the Gold Coast) beyond the river network.

competitive_landscape: Brisbane City Council runs the CityCat / CityHopper / Cross River network under Translink. Navier is a passenger-only foiling layer above the existing service, complementing the all-electric CityCat program rather than competing with it.
regulatory_note: Strict low-wake operation and no-foil zones are required through the residential and rowing reaches of the river; foiling is used only where the channel and wake rules allow.
